survey: A DJ controller with a pair of over-ear headphones in front of it on an orange floor. The controller is a rounded blue slab seen from above at a three-quarter angle, standing on short blue feet: two at the front corners and a rear one visible behind the headphones. On top are two jog platters set into round wells. They fit ellipses with width ratios of about 0.59 and 0.64, with matching tilt, which agrees with the top seen at a slant. Behind them, a raised strip holds three knobs. A raised centre panel has two vertical slots, and each green fader cap sits in its own slot. There are three square pads under the left platter, three under the right platter, and three pads under the centre panel. Every control sits on or in the deck surface. The headphones stand on their cups in front of the controller's right front corner. The headband arcs up and in front of the controller's front edge. It has an outer band, a cyan top pad, and a square slider block at each end. Each block joins the top of its cup. The far (left) cup shows its cushion opening toward the viewer, and the near (right) cup shows its outer plate. That is correct, because the cups face each other: the viewer looks into the far cup and at the back of the near cup. Both cups touch the floor and cast shadows. Nothing floats, no thin part ends in the air, and there are no extra or missing parts beyond fair simplification. The wireless headphones need no cable, and the missing crossfader is a simplification.
